---
title: "How do I load a CSV into R and check that it worked?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I load a CSV into R and check that it worked?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Identify the CSV file path.

2. Use read.csv() and store the result.

3. Inspect head(), str(), names(), and nrow().

## Runnable example

```{r}
# Example: make a temporary CSV so this script runs anywhere.
source_data <- data.frame(day=c(1,2,3), rainfall_mm=c(4,0,9))
file <- tempfile(fileext=".csv")
write.csv(source_data,file,row.names=FALSE)
d <- read.csv(file)
print(head(d))
str(d)
print(names(d))
print(nrow(d))
unlink(file)
```

## Interpret the result

The sample has three rows and a numeric rainfall column. Replace the temporary file path with the location of your own CSV. Never assume the imported columns have the intended types.

## Check before applying this to real data

Inspect the column names, data types, row count, and whether numbers were imported as text.
